name: gcal-block-sweep-peter

deploy.description: Peter's copy of gcal-block-sweep. Daily horizon backstop, coming-week reconciler and manual backfill for Peter's two-way calendar-blocking pair (scw-events-to-workflowers-block-peter / workflowers-events-to-scw-busy-peter). Those Zaps refuse to create mirrors for occurrences starting more than 30 days out, and Zapier's polling dedupe means a skipped occurrence never re-fires on its own — so this sweep scans the week rolling INTO the horizon (days 23..30) each morning, in both directions, and creates any mirror Peter's GCal Sync Map table says is missing. It also reconciles the coming week (days 0..7), which is where every change to an already-mirrored occurrence propagates: source gone/cancelled or no longer block-worthy (declined, Free, all-day) -> delete the mirror and mark the row deleted; source moved or renamed -> update the mirror and refresh the row; a row previously marked deleted whose source is block-worthy again is revived. Manual runs take a window override for the cutover backfill ({"from_days":0,"to_days":30}), a reconcile_days override (0 disables) and a dryRun flag. The inherited cleanup_notion_blocks flag is inert for Peter. ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from Dennis's copy (Peter, 2026-09-15): in the scw_to_wf direction, SCW events whose Google eventType is focusTime, outOfOffice or workingLocation are never mirrored, and the reconcile pass unmirrors one whose source has turned into such a type.

trigger.authentication_note: Schedule by Zapier needs no connection. Both of Peter's Google credentials are --connections aliases because the workflow reads AND writes both calendars.
trigger.trigger_note: Daily at 7:00 AM account time, weekends included — same tick as Dennis's gcal-block-sweep. The tick payload's `id` field IS the fire time as an RFC 3339 timestamp — the workflow uses it as its deterministic clock, so scheduled runs never read Date.now().
trigger.manual_run_note: Cutover backfill: trigger-workflow <id> --input '{"from_days":0,"to_days":30,"reconcile_days":30,"dryRun":true}' first and eyeball the counts, then again without dryRun. Steady-state cost: ~4 search tasks/day (2 create-window + 2 reconcile-window) plus one task per occurrence that newly rolls into the horizon and one per mirror created, revived, updated or deleted by reconciliation.

connections_note: gcal_wf is Peter's work.flowers Google Calendar connection ('peter@work.flowers'); gcal_scw is Peter's SCW one ('pgao@securecodewarrior.com'). Both are read (event_v2 window search on the source side) and written (detailed_event on the destination side). Never Dennis's ids (02a752ba-… / 02cb5353-…).
sharing_note: Peter's connections (02b0ea0a-… work.flowers, 02edd3ce-… SCW) and the GCal Sync Map (Peter) table 01M2HT9XPZEASFV09J4A3QTDGT are owned by Peter's own Zapier profile, not the CI identity. The publish pipeline's CI identity must be able to use all three, so they are shared with the work.flowers account before merge — see gcal-block-sweep-peter/README.md. Shared on: 2026-09-25.

tables.01M2HT9XPZEASFV09J4A3QTDGT: GCal Sync Map (Peter) — source occurrence id -> mirror event id, both directions. SHARED with Peter's four trigger Zaps, never with Dennis's: read to skip everything already mapped (free), written with a row for each mirror this sweep creates. Columns: Source Event ID (f1), Mirror Event ID (f2), Direction (f3), Status (f4), Start (f5), End (f6), Summary (f7), Source Updated (f8).

description: Peter's copy: daily sweep that mirrors calendar events newly rolling into the 30-day blocking horizon, reconciles the coming week against Peter's source calendars (updating moved/renamed mirrors, deleting mirrors whose occurrence vanished or stopped being block-worthy, reviving ones that are block-worthy again), and doubles as the manual cutover backfill. ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from Dennis's copy (Peter, 2026-09-15): in the scw_to_wf direction, SCW events whose Google eventType is focusTime, outOfOffice or workingLocation are never mirrored, and the reconcile pass unmirrors one whose source has turned into such a type.
